throwdownCode.description: The Throwdown the client wants to join.

playerId.description: Stable participant id for this match: the ArcAid user id, or a fakeclient label.

publicKey.description: Ed25519 public key, 32 raw bytes, base64.

rig.description: The player's declared rig, for provenance (ArcAid badge, never a gate).

tableName.description: Human name of the table or ROM set.

tableHash.description: SHA-256 of the ORIGINAL .vpx (never the patched copy), or of the arcade ROM zip.

romName.description: PinMAME ROM set name (e.g. mm_109c) or arcade ROM name; null for originals.

romHash.description: SHA-256 of the ROM zip; null for originals.

physicsHash.description: Hash of the physics-relevant table settings; null when not computed.

recipeVersion.description: Castcade patch recipe version applied to this table (ADR 0004); null for arcade.

sidecarHash.description: SHA-256 of the generated sidecar .vbs; proves both players run the same patch.

emulatorVersion.description: VPX or RetroArch core version string.

game.description: Everything that must match between participants for a fair match. The host compares these at HELLO.

ballEndReady.description: A13: whether the sender's companion can report this table's ball ends (it follows the table's hook journal): false when a table is open and it cannot (not patched, an original table, an unreadable machine). Absent: unknown (no table open yet, or a companion from before A13).

stance.description: A17: Play or Watch at the next start. Absent: play.

proof.description: A17: the sender's signature over canonicalJson({hello: true, lobby, player, seq}) with the key in `participant.publicKey`: the lobby's code, its player id, and this envelope's own `seq`. A lobby that still holds a place for that player with that key takes the HELLO as that member's return when the signature verifies and the `seq` is above the last it took from them; without it such a HELLO is refused (`duplicate_player`). Ignored for a player the lobby holds no place for.

description: client -> host. First message on a connection.
